newsitem.title: USA: Arafat laments dealing with Netanyahu, not Rabin.
newsitem.headline: Arafat laments dealing with Netanyahu, not Rabin.

text.p: Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said in remarks broadcast on Wednesday that he wished he were still dealing with the late Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin rather than his successor, Benjamin Netanyahu.
Arafat accused Netanyahu of kowtowing to "fanatic" Jewish groups and said the Mideast peace process was in serious danger as a result.
"We have to be very careful because peace is very important," he said in an interview taped on Tuesday night in New York with the NBC television programme "Today."
"Prime Minister Rabin, whom we lost, he paid his life for the sake of this peace, " Arafat added. Asked if he wished he were still dealing with Rabin, Arafat replied in imperfect English: "Definite."
Rabin was assassinated in November 1995 by a right-wing Israeli Jewish extremist opposed to the Rabin government's policy of trading occupied Arab lands for peace.
Arafat blasted Netanyahu's plan to build a new Jewish neighbourhood in East Jerusalem, which Israel seized along with other Arab territory in the 1967 Middle East War.

"I am not asking for the moon," he said. "I am asking (for implementation of) what has been signed," a reference to Israeli-Palestinian pacts. After meeting with Arafat on Monday, President Bill Clinton criticised the Israeli construction plan, saying it "builds mistrust."
Arafat arrived at the United Nations in New York late on Tuesday for a gala reception of well over 1,000 people sponsored by Palestinian-Americans from the New York area.
On Wednesday he will brief the U.N. Security Council shortly before it debates Israel's East Jerusalem construction plan.
